agent: Claude Code (CLAUDE.md, this repository) — rename execution_policy/GUIDED to skip_policy/ADVISORY
summary_for_principal: You flagged that "guided" already means something specific elsewhere — an agent calling in for the current step, doing the work, and reporting back, one step at a time. That is in fact how this whole engine has always worked, for every run, regardless of any setting; there was no gap to build. The actual problem was a name collision: the spec's own vocabulary had reused the word "guided" for a narrower, unrelated setting (whether a person may skip a minor step). Renamed that setting from execution_policy: STRICT | GUIDED to skip_policy: STRICT | ADVISORY, everywhere it appears — the format's rulebook, the schema, the code, and the tests. This frees "guided" to keep its one meaning going forward. Pure rename: no behaviour changed, and the full test suite (294 tests) still passes unchanged. Recorded as a new decision (D16) in the rulebook's own decision log, alongside the two decisions it touches.
